q: (Affectionately addressing Rasulullaah ﷺ according to his dress at the time, Allaah says,)
O you wrapped in a cloth
v.s: O you who wraps himself [in clothing]
v.c: O you wrapped ˹in your clothes˺!

v.s: Arise [to pray] the night, except for a little -
v.c: Stand all night ˹in prayer˺ except a little—

q: half the night or slightly less
(than half, such as a third of the night)...
v.s: Half of it - or subtract from it a little
v.c: ˹pray˺ half the night, or a little less,

q: (time to the half, making it two-thirds).
(and steadily so that each letter is distinct and accurately pronounced).
v.s: Or add to it, and recite the Qur’ān with measured recitation.
v.c: or a little more—and recite the Quran ˹properly˺ in a measured way.

q: Verily We shall soon cast a weighty
v.s: Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word.
v.c: ˹For˺ We will soon send upon you a weighty revelation.

q: (but most effective for controlling the Nafs)
(because it is a time when one is free of duties and disturbances).
v.s: Indeed, the hours of the night are more effective for concurrence [of heart and tongue] and more suitable for words.
v.c: Indeed, worship in the night is more impactful and suitable for recitation.

q: (and will be unable to devote your attention exclusively for worship during the day. The night is therefore best for this purpose).
v.s: Indeed, for you by day is prolonged occupation.
v.c: For during the day you are over-occupied ˹with worldly duties˺.

q: Mention the name of your Rabb
to focus your attention solely on Him.
v.s: And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with [complete] devotion.
v.c: ˹Always˺ remember the Name of your Lord, and devote yourself to Him wholeheartedly.

q: He is the Rabb of the East and the West. There is no Ilaah but Him, so adopt Him as your guardian
v.s: [He is] the Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Disposer of [your] affairs.
v.c: ˹He is the˺ Lord of the east and the west. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him, so take Him ˹alone˺ as a Trustee of Affairs.

q: separate from them in a most pleasant manner
(without fighting them and without the desire for revenge). (This ayat is Makki revealed before Hijraat. The order of jihaad came in Madinah.)
v.s: And be patient over what they say and avoid them with gracious avoidance.
v.c: Be patient ˹O Prophet˺ with what they say, and depart from them courteously.

q: and grant them grace for a while
(bear with them until they learn their lesson the hard way).
v.s: And leave Me with [the matter of] the deniers, those of ease [in life], and allow them respite a little.
v.c: And leave to Me the deniers—the people of luxury—and bear with them for a little while.

v.s: Indeed, with Us [for them] are shackles and burning fire.
v.c: ˹For˺ We certainly have shackles, a ˹raging˺ Fire,

q: ...food that gets stuck in the throat
(cannot be swallowed because of its terrible taste and texture)
v.s: And food that chokes and a painful punishment -
v.c: choking food, and a painful punishment ˹in store for them˺

q: when the earth and mountains will shake
and the mountains will be reduced to
v.s: On the Day the earth and the mountains will convulse and the mountains will become a heap of sand pouring down.
v.c: on the Day the earth and mountains will shake ˹violently˺, and mountains will be ˹reduced to˺ dunes of shifting sand.

q: Verily We have sent a Rasool
(to your actions so that he may testify on the Day of Qiyaamah)
just as We sent a Rasool
v.s: Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger as a witness upon you just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger.
v.c: Indeed, We have sent to you a messenger as a witness over you, just as We sent a messenger to Pharaoh.

q: Fir'oun refused to obey the Rasool so We seized
v.s: But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a ruinous seizure.
v.c: But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a stern grip.

v.s: Then how can you fear, if you disbelieve, a Day that will make the children white-haired?
v.c: If you ˹pagans˺ persist in disbelief, then how will you guard yourselves against ˹the horrors of˺ a Day which will turn children’s hair grey?

q: The sky will be split apart on that day. His
v.s: The heaven will break apart therefrom; ever is His promise fulfilled.
v.c: It will ˹even˺ cause the sky to split apart. His promise ˹of judgment˺ must be fulfilled.

q: is advice indeed. So whoever wishes to do so, should adopt a path
v.s: Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way.
v.c: Surely this is a reminder. So let whoever wills take the ˹Right˺ Way to their Lord.

q: (In trying to put into practice verses 3 and 4 above, Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah ﵃ found it tedious to precisely calculate two-thirds, half or one-third of the night. Fearing that they should miscalculate and fail to stand for the stipulated periods, the Sahabah ﵃ therefore stood in salaah almost the entire night. As a result of this exertion, their feet used to swell and they grew extremely pale. Taking pity on them, Allaah revealed the verse saying,)
Verily your Rabb knows that you
close to two-thirds of the night,
night and the day. He knows that you are unable to precisely calculate
(the duration of each portion of the night)
so He has turned to you in mercy. Therefore,
(instead of trying to recite too much)
recite that part of the Qur'aan
(stand in Tahajjud only as long as you can manage).
Allaah knows that some of you may fall ill, others will travel in the world in search of Allaah's bounty
and others will fight in Allaah's path.
(In each case, they will be unable to perform Tahajjud as they do at home.)
(Although Tahajjud is not obligatory, do not neglect to)
salaah, pay zakaah and give to Allaah a good loan (spend in charity for Allaah's pleasure). Whatever good you send ahead for yourselves
you will find it with Allaah in a better and more rewarding state. Seek forgiveness from Allaah. Verily Allaah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
v.s: Indeed, your Lord knows, [O Muhammad], that you stand [in prayer] almost two thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it, and [so do] a group of those with you. And God determines [the extent of] the night and the day. He has known that you [Muslims] will not be able to do it and has turned to you in forgiveness, so recite what is easy [for you] of the Qur’ān. He has known that there will be among you those who are ill and others traveling throughout the land seeking [something] of the bounty of God and others fighting for the cause of God. So recite what is easy from it and establish prayer and give zakāh and loan God a goodly loan. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with God. It is better and greater in reward. And seek forgiveness of God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
v.c: Surely your Lord knows that you ˹O Prophet˺ stand ˹in prayer˺ for nearly two-thirds of the night, or ˹sometimes˺ half of it, or a third, as do some of those with you. Allah ˹alone˺ keeps a ˹precise˺ measure of the day and night. He knows that you ˹believers˺ are unable to endure this, and has turned to you in mercy. So recite ˹in prayer˺ whatever you can from the Quran. He knows that some of you will be sick, some will be travelling throughout the land seeking Allah’s bounty, and some fighting in the cause of Allah. So recite whatever you can from it. And ˹continue to˺ perform ˹regular˺ prayers, pay alms-tax, and lend to Allah a good loan. Whatever good you send forth for yourselves, you will find it with Allah far better and more rewarding. And seek Allah’s forgiveness. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
